Article Title: Amazon may spend $7 billion on AI startup Decart that Anthropic walked away from after offering $6 billion
Article Text:
Amazon eyes key AI infrastructure technology

What Decart does

Anthropic stepped back after due diligence

Amazon is reportedly in talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart in a deal valued around $7 billion, a move that would strengthen the tech giant's position in the rapidly expanding AI infrastructure market, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The proposed acquisition comes just weeks after AI firm Anthropic reportedly decided against pursuing a takeover of Decart following due diligence on a potential $6 billion deal. For those unaware, Decart is a San Francisco-based company which has developed software which enable the developers to switch more easily between different AI chips, a capability that has become increasingly important as demand for computing power surges amid the AI boom.Amazon has developed its own custom AI chip, Trainium3, to compete with Nvidia, which dominates the market for AI graphics processors. The Journal has reported that Amazon Web Services gave Decart early access to the chip in 2025 after meeting the company and being impressed by its founders. Decart's software could help customers adopt Trainium alongside other hardware.If completed, the deal would be larger than Amazon's $6.5 billion purchase of the MGM studio in 2022.It would still be smaller than the roughly $11 billion deal for Starlink rival Globalstar that Amazon announced earlier this year. The Israeli outlet Calcalist reported earlier this month that Decart was in advanced talks to be sold to a major technology company.Decart's software makes it easier for developers to switch between different AI chips, a capability that is becoming more important as companies race to secure computing power. The company, founded in 2023 by Israeli engineers Dean and Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev, is based in San Francisco. It is also developing "world models" called Lucy and Oasis, which can generate and simulate real-world 3-D environments.According to PitchBook, Decart has raised more than $400 million from investors including Sequoia Capital, Benchmark and Radical Ventures. It was valued at nearly $4 billion in May, so a $7 billion price would be a sharp jump in a few months.The deal follows an earlier near-miss. Bloomberg reported in September that Anthropic had decided against acquiring Decart after exploring a deal and performing due diligence, and that the companies might still look for other ways to collaborate. Anthropic had been in talks to buy Decart for about $6 billion, though nothing had been finalized. It would have been Anthropic's largest acquisition to date.Reports differ on how firm the $6 billion figure was. Bloomberg described talks at about that level, not a signed or formal offer, so "offered $6 billion" may overstate it. One outlet said Decart's team would have joined Anthropic's inference and performance organization, but I haven't seen the reasons for Anthropic's decision confirmed by either company.
Article Summary: Anthropic stepped back after due diligence on a potential $6 billion deal. Decart's software makes it easier for developers to switch between different AI chips. Amazon has developed its own custom AI chip, Trainium3, to compete with Nvidia, which dominates the market for AI graphics processors.

Article Title: FBI 'goes to' Canada in search of hackers that stole data of thousands of its employees, arrests Canadian cybersecurity expert; Kash Patel says: We will continue to ...
Article Text:
FBI Director Kash Patel/Image: AP

“We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate.”

FBI arrests Canadian cybersecurity expert over ShinyHunters attack

FBI employee data exposed in cyberattack

ShinyHunters faces international law enforcement action

FBI has arrested a Canadian cybersecurity expert. A New York Times report, citing people familiar with the matter, says the FBI arrested Edward Dubrovsky in Pennsylvania. He is suspected of helping carry out a cyberattack that exposed sensitive information about thousands of FBI employees. According to his LinkedIn profile, Dubrovsky specialises in negotiating ransom payments with cybercriminals. The arrest is part of the bureau's efforts to pursue members of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which claimed responsibility for stealing personal information from the FBI's jobs portal.FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the arrest and said the agency would continue working with international partners to disrupt the group and its associates. He said:Dubrovsky faces a conspiracy-to-commit-extortion charge, according to federal court records in Philadelphia, while the details of the charges remain under seal in Texas. He is expected to be transported to Texas to face the charges.The report claimed that the FBI considers Dubrovsky, who has worked with companies affected by cyberattacks, a primary co-conspirator in the attack on FBI data, citing people familiar with the matter.He recently published a book titled Cyber Extortion Strategic Response.The FBI has been investigating the breach after ShinyHunters claimed it had stolen information about agency personnel from its jobs portal. The group threatened further consequences if the bureau withdrew an advisory warning the public about its cyberattacks, although it later backed away from that threat.The stolen information reportedly included home addresses, Social Security numbers, sensitive job assignments and details about employees' family members. Following the breach, the FBI told its workforce that it was operating under the assumption that all employees had been affected.Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI's cyber division, said an internal review traced the incident to a security failure involving a third-party platform. According to the bureau, a contractor had failed to implement a security patch specifically issued to protect the system. Reuters previously reported that the contractor worked for Accenture.Leatherman said the FBI had removed the contractor and taken steps to reduce further risks. He also confirmed that investigators had made multiple arrests as part of the investigation.The arrest follows other international efforts to investigate the hacking group. Last month, authorities in the Netherlands arrested a 24-year-old suspected of affiliation with ShinyHunters, though the group denied knowing him.Security researchers describe ShinyHunters as a loose network of English-speaking hackers operating across several countries. The group has targeted organisations through third-party vendors and cloud-based platforms, often seeking payments in exchange for promises not to release stolen information.Leatherman said the group is believed to have breached more than 140 organisations and extorted $70 million since last year.
Article Summary: FBI arrests Canadian cybersecurity expert over ShinyHunters attack. Edward Dubrovsky is suspected of helping carry out a cyberattack that exposed sensitive information about thousands of FBI employees. The FBI has been investigating the breach after Shinyhunters claimed it had stolen information about agency personnel from its jobs portal.

Article Title: H-1B Visa: US government has suspended PERMS for Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Cognizant employees: What this means for Green Card applicants, older and others
Article Text:
What is PERM and why does it matter

What does it mean for H-1B workers

The unknowns that matter most

Why the suspension matters

The US government’s decision to suspend several major technology firms, including Infosys , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, Cognizant, HCLTech, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the PERM labour certification programme could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. The move, announced by the US Department of Labor, prevents the affected companies from filing new PERM applications and processing pending PERM cases. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs. Vice President JD Vance, who announced the action jointly with Sonderling, called H-1B workers "foreign indentured servants" and the companies "visa mills," arguing the practice has shut Americans out of the job market. An investigation was also ordered into the J-1 visa programme for research scholars at nine major universities, including Yale, Harvard, Stanford and Caltech.Workers who haven't started PERM. If their employer cannot file a new PERM application, they may have to wait before beginning the standard employer-sponsored green card route. They also cannot establish a priority date through a new PERM filing during the suspension.The priority date sets a worker's place in the green card queue. That matters especially for Indian professionals, who already face lengthy queues because of high demand and country-based numerical limits.Workers with a pending PERM. The Labor Department has said it will not process pending applications involving the named companies during the suspension. In practice, long-pending cases that were already waiting could be frozen where they stand.Workers with an approved PERM or I-140. It is unclear whether already approved labor certifications or immigrant petitions will be affected, and officials have not given guidance. Lawyers who analyzed earlier suspensions at other companies said approved PERM certifications, approved I-140 petitions and existing H-1B status were not wiped out. That may not carry over to this action, so affected workers should ask their attorneys.Visa and work status. A PERM suspension is not the same as cancelling H-1B visas. It does not by itself change a worker's current status.It’s important to note that this decision of the US government does not cancel the existing H-1B visa s. Also, the employees presently working on a valid H-1B visa in the IS can continue to work as per their current visa approvals. But the workers relying on employer-sponsored Green Cards may face some major delays in obtaining permanent residency. Also, the workers whose PERM applications are pending, or who were planning to start the process, could witness delay in immigration timelines.Officials have not said how long the suspension will last or how the companies can get it lifted. Under Labor Department regulations, an initial suspension during a fraud investigation can run up to 180 days and be extended while the investigation is unresolved, so lawyers warn employers not to assume processing resumes automatically.For H-1B holders, time is a concern. Under federal law, H-1B workers can generally extend beyond the six-year limit only if a PERM was filed at least a year before that limit is reached. Workers who cannot get a PERM filed may need to consider other options, such as changing employers. This is general background, not guidance specific to this suspension, and an immigration attorney should advise on individual cases.The action marks one of the most significant recent restrictions on the employment-based Green Card process for major technology companies. While workers can continue to hold H-1B status, the freeze effectively blocks a crucial pathway to permanent residency for employees of the affected firms, raising uncertainty for thousands of foreign professionals awaiting Green Cards.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended the PERM labour certification programme. The move could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg tells investors Meta’s AI investments are accelerating every part of the business; and to IRS, Meta says: Our AI data centers are an experiment that could fail
Article Text:
Meta’s AI data centers: a success for investors, an ‘experiment’ for the IRS

How Meta turned Nvidia AI chips into 'pilot models' for tax purposes

Meta's own filings warn the AI tax savings could be overturned

The tax credit's original sponsor says it was meant for people, not hardware

Mark Zuckerberg has spent two years telling investors that Meta's AI spending is paying off across Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook. When the company files its taxes, it tells the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) a very different story. According to a New York Times report, Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work.That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit, a break Congress created in 1981 to reward risky innovation. The payoff has been big. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023, the year before it started using it for data centers. The NYT found Meta is now the largest beneficiary of the credit among publicly traded companies.In its tax filings, Meta classifies its multibillion-dollar AI data centers as "pilot models." Under the rules, supplies qualify for the credit only when they are part of an experimental effort, not regular business. So Meta argues the costly chips it buys from Nvidia and others belong to an experiment and deserve the discount.The idea came from an employee overseeing the data center build-out in mid-2024, the report says. Some in Meta's finance team doubted it would survive scrutiny, since the IRS has previously rejected claims for proven, commercially available equipment. Lawyers Meta consulted pointed to a 2021 ruling that denied the credit to an Indiana shipbuilder, which held that simply building a new product isn't enough. After a few months of deliberation, Meta began tagging chips bound for AI data centers differently from those going to standard ones.Andre Shevchuck, a research tax credit specialist at advisory firm BPM, called the experimental label "kind of wild and out there."Meta's accountants appear to share some of that doubt. Since the strategy began, the company's unrecognized tax benefits, the money set aside in case tax authorities win a challenge, have climbed 45% to $18.74 billion from $12.9 billion. The first reason listed in its annual filing is uncertainty around research tax credits.Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft also report over $1 billion a year in research credits. None has flagged it as a risk to investors.Meta spokesman Andy Stone said the company invested $200 billion in R&D over five years, $57 billion of it last year, and uses incentives Congress set up for this kind of domestic investment. He called unrecognized tax benefits a mandated accounting measure of uncertainty. Meta declined to explain what makes its data centers experimental.This isn't Meta's only research credit fight with the IRS. The agency is trying to claw back $355 million after Meta counted $4.1 billion in stock options Zuckerberg exercised in 2013 as a research expense. Separately, the IRS wants nearly $16 billion over profits it says Meta shifted to the Cayman Islands.James Shannon, the former Massachusetts congressman who sponsored the credit, told the NYT it was meant to back researchers and knowledge, not manufacturing. Meta's use, he said, goes "way, way beyond" what anyone imagined.The Joint Committee on Taxation estimated the credit would cost the US government $32.1 billion in 2025. Meta alone accounts for more than a tenth of that, on a bet its CEO keeps telling investors is already working.
Article Summary: Report: Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work. That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023.

Article Title: Sigma launches 50-120mm F2.8 telephoto zoom in India, 16-300mm superzoom gets a new mount
Article Text:
A palm-sized F2.8 telephoto for APS-C shooters.

Nikon Z shooters get Sigma's 18.8x superzoom in November

Sigma has two new APS-C lenses on the way in India, and both are aimed at photographers who would rather not keep swapping glass. The 50-120mm F2.8 DC OS | Contemporary goes on sale on October 22, while the 16-300mm F3.5-6.7 DC OS | Contemporary, already sold for other mounts, reaches Nikon Z cameras on November 5.The 50-120mm is the all-new one of the pair. It brings a constant F2.8 aperture to an APS-C telephoto zoom, covering roughly 75-180mm in full-frame terms, in a body just 99mm long and 390g in its Sony E-mount version. It will be available for Sony E, Fujifilm X and Canon RF cameras.It also completes the company's F2.8 zoom trio for crop-sensor cameras. With the existing 10-18mm F2.8 and 18-50mm F2.8, all three lenses together weigh under a kilogram and run from ultra-wide to telephoto.Inside are one FLD, three SLD and four aspherical elements. A High-response Linear Actuator (HLA) handles autofocus, focus breathing is kept low for video, and stabilisation is rated at 6.5 stops at 50mm and 4.5 stops at 120mm. The focus mode and OS switches are gone entirely, so those settings now live in the camera body. It also gets dust and splash resistance, plus a water- and oil-repellent front coating.The 16-300mm is built as a one-lens kit. Its 18.8x zoom range is, by Sigma's count, a world first for an autofocus interchangeable lens on mirrorless cameras, and it focuses close enough for 1:2 magnification.Stabilisation is rated at 6 stops at 16mm and 4.5 stops at 300mm. For Nikon, AF drive and communication speed have been tuned to the Z mount, with support for continuous AF, in-camera aberration correction on compatible bodies, and a rubber-sealed mount.Both lenses follow the full-frame 85mm F1.2 DG | Art and 20-60mm F2.8-4 DG | Contemporary, which went on sale in India on September 30. For APS-C users, the choice now comes down to one lens that reaches 300mm, or three that hold F2.8 all the way to 120mm.
Article Summary: Nikon Z shooters get Sigma's 18.8x superzoom in November. 50-120mm F2.8 DC OS | Contemporary goes on sale in India on October 22. 16-300mm F3.5-6.7 DC OS| Contemporary reaches Nikon Z cameras on November 5.

Article Title: ‘Let's get to work’: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman after Satya Nadella backs ‘emergency brake’ for AI models
Article Text:
Microsoft AI Chief Mustafa Suleyman

Satya Nadella’s ‘emergency brake’ plan

Designing for observability over blind trust

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has thrown his weight behind company chief executive Satya Nadella ’s call for mandatory safeguards on advanced artificial intelligence (AI), declaring that containing superintelligence is an achievable technical hurdle the tech industry must tackle immediately. Reacting to Nadella’s safety proposals, Suleyman emphasised that humanity has successfully tamed high-risk innovations throughout history, framing AI oversight as a standard engineering milestone rather than an unsolvable dilemma.“Super Intelligence must be contained... Today, this is an engineering and governance challenge. And it isn't new. We've done it with planes, cars, nuclear materials, food safety, medicines... and everything else. Let's get to work!” Suleyman wrote in a post on X (formerly Twitter).Suleyman’s remarks follow an extensive position statement published on X by Nadella on Saturday, where the Microsoft chief urged developers to equip advanced AI systems with hard boundaries, external oversight, and a literal “emergency brake” allowing authorised operators to halt or disconnect a system in the middle of an operation.Nadella argued that unpredictable generative algorithms cannot be left unchecked and must be insulated by rigid, deterministic software guardrails.“We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient,” Nadella wrote.He went further by suggesting that frontier systems, whether closed-source proprietary platforms or open-weight releases, should be approached with the same defensive mindset companies apply to internal security vulnerabilities: “Treating frontier closed and open weight models like insider risks is a way to build such a system.”Outlining a technical blueprint for the superintelligence era, Nadella argued that safety frameworks should be built on core “principles of observability” rather than blind reliance on a model’s good behaviour. His proposed framework hinges on six primary operational requirements, including model diversity, human-readable footprints, continuous system testing, independent controls and auditability, containment and mandatory incident disclosure.
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has thrown his weight behind Satya Nadella’s call for mandatory safeguards on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) He said that containing superintelligence is an achievable technical hurdle the tech industry must tackle immediately. Suley man emphasised that humanity has successfully tamed high-risk innovations throughout history.

Article Title: Swiss watches that Google's top execs are reportedly 'obsessed with,' and made Tudor build a special edition for them
Article Text:
Google employees got Tudor to build them their own Swiss watch

Tudor needs at least 40 buyers before it customises a watch

OpenAI, Palantir and Uber staff have their own limited-edition Tudors

Custom tech-company Tudor watches are selling for double their retail price

Silicon Valley has a new way to flex, and at Google , it comes with a Swiss movement and a Tudor logo. In August, a post showing custom Tudor watches built for Googlers started circulating on X, and staffers at OpenAI, Palantir, Uber and Perplexity were soon replying with photos of their own company-branded timepieces. The Google edition is based on the Tudor Pelagos, a titanium diver that retails for around $4,500 (roughly Rs 4.3 lakh). Google does not hand these out. Like most of these watches, it was ordered by an internal group of watch collectors, paid for out of pocket, and is usually available only to members of the group that commissioned it.Tudor, Rolex’s sister brand, runs a customisation programme with a minimum order of 40 watches, according to the managing editor of a luxury watch news site. Production takes about six months. Employee collector groups do the work of rounding up enough interested buyers, and each member pays full retail price.That setup keeps runs small and designs private. A watch made for one company’s collector group tends to stay within that group, so every edition is rare by default.OpenAI’s head of applied research, Boris Power, posted the company’s version, which has “Good Research Takes Time” engraved on the caseback.The same slogan appears on T-shirts OpenAI sells, and Power has said Tudor made 400 of these with OpenAI’s logo on the dial.Palantir’s strategic engagement head, Eliano Younes, said the company’s run was limited to 468 pieces, with a barely noticeable Palantir logo on the dial. Uber engineer Alex Feng shared a caseback marked 1/100, the first watch in a batch of 100. A former Facebook employee admitted he regretted not buying every custom model made during his six years there.Tudor is not the only maker involved. Adobe’s watch club is working with British brand Studio Underd0g on 128 branded pieces at about $1,200 (around Rs 1.2 lakh) each. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman went further, commissioning just seven watches from Swiss maker Vanguart, based on a model that starts at $180,000 (about Rs 1.7 crore), with “COMPUTE IS DESTINY” engraved around the rotor.Rarity carries a premium. A Google-themed Tudor featuring Chrome’s offline dinosaur sold for over $10,000 (about Rs 9.6 lakh) at auction earlier this year, while an Apple “pirate” edition drew a $13,500 (around Rs 13 lakh) bid. A Meta-branded Tudor Black Bay 54 has attracted bids as high as $10,500 (about Rs 10 lakh), against a standard price of $4,725 (roughly Rs 4.6 lakh).Not every branded watch fetches those numbers, and one online watch auctioneer pointed out that some buyers simply find them ugly. For the people ordering them, the draw is belonging. An Adobe designer who owns about 40 watches described these pieces as a ticket into an insider club.Google’s own chief is the odd one out. Sundar Pichai’s most talked-about watch moment came in 2022, when he wore an unreleased Pixel Watch on stage. His employees, it seems, would rather wear the company logo on a Swiss movement.
Article Summary: Tudor, Rolex’s sister brand, runs a customisation programme with a minimum order of 40 watches. Employee collector groups do the work of rounding up enough interested buyers, and each member pays full retail price. A Google-themed Tudor featuring Chrome's offline dinosaur sold for over $10,000 at auction earlier this year.

Article Title: Wisconsin couple rejects $131,000 offer for proposed data centre power line that threatens their trees, six buildings and puts 130-foot tower near their driveway
Article Text:
Pennsylvania data centre (Representative AI image)

Proposed power line threatens trees and buildings

​Homeowner questions $131,000 compensation offer

​Dispute over data centre power line continues

Wisconsin homeowner Jerry Zelenka has rejected a $131,000 offer from American Transmission Company (ATC). The money was offered for a proposed power line that would cross his property in Fredonia, Wisconsin, to supply electricity to a planned data centre in nearby Port Washington. Zelenka said the latest proposal calls for clearing mature trees, demolishing six buildings and placing a 130-foot transmission tower near his driveway.​The company has offered $81,000 in compensation for the property impacts, along with an additional $50,000 one-time payment if he signs an agreement now. The 75-year-old homeowner, who bought the land with his wife in 1990, said the proposed changes would leave their house standing while removing much of the property they have built and maintained over the years.Zelenka said ATC's latest proposal follows an earlier application that, according to him, the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin deemed incomplete. The company has since submitted a new application with revised plans and routes.​Under the current proposal, Zelenka said, a stretch measuring about 1,000 feet long and 75 feet wide would be cleared of trees and vegetation. The affected trees include cedar, oak, ash, elm and black walnut.He also said the project would require removing a shed, chicken coop, hog barn, antique barn, garage, and machine shed.​“The point is that everything from that fence all the way to the road is clear-cut,” Zelenka said. “And after they clear-cut it, then they want to spray herbicide and just kill everything between my house and the highway.”​The proposed tower and high-voltage lines would also change the property's surroundings, potentially affecting its value.​“My house is right there. The only thing that’s left standing is the house,” he said.Zelenka said the proposed compensation wouldn't cover the cost of replacing the buildings or adequately account for the impact on the property's value. He also objected to the additional payment being conditional on signing an agreement immediately.“You know, the bribe in a sense is that if I were to sign up now, they’re offering $50,000 more,” Zelenka said.The homeowner said relocating was not a realistic option for him and his 73-year-old wife, who has advanced Parkinson’s disease. The couple built their home after buying the land in the winter of 1990, spending nine months on the house while living in a shed.​Zelenka said he would not voluntarily accept the proposal and raised concerns that ATC could use eminent domain to acquire the property if they could not reach an agreement.​“If they decide they’re going to go this way, they can file for eminent domain, they’ll condemn the property, and there’s nothing I can do about it,” Zelenka said. “Then they’ll make an offer for whatever they feel is acceptable, and my only option at that point is I can fight them in court for a higher value, but I can’t stop the land seizure.”Zelenka questioned whether the proposed transmission line qualifies for eminent domain, arguing it would primarily serve a private data centre rather than the general public. He said two neighbouring property owners who are attorneys are challenging the issue in federal court. The legal outcome and the project's final route remain uncertain.The homeowner also said changing proposals and compensation offers made ATC's plans hard to understand.​“The thing that’s really frustrating is trying to get the truth or accurate information,” he said. “First we get offers and then the offers are pulled and we think they’re routing another way… then, oop… now they’re sending new offers.”​Zelenka said he intends to continue opposing the proposed route rather than accept the compensation and fight it in court.
Article Summary: Wisconsin homeowner Jerry Zelenka has rejected a $131,000 offer from American Transmission Company (ATC) The money was offered for a proposed power line that would cross his property in Fredonia, Wisconsin, to supply electricity to a planned data centre in nearby Port Washington. The latest proposal calls for clearing mature trees, demolishing six buildings and placing a 130-foot transmission tower.

Article Title: After investing $65 billion in Sam Altman's OpenAl, Japan's richest man Masayoshi Son is seeking $100 billion to fund other AI projects
Article Text:
What are the key elements of proposed structure

Softbank’s exposure to OpenAI and debt load

SoftBank founder and Japan’s richest person, Masayoshi Son, is seeking up to $100 billion from Gulf investors to set up a new fund designed to buy out traditional businesses and overhaul their operations using artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics, a report has said. SoftBank is facing mounting market scrutiny over its $65 billion commitment to Sam Altman’s OpenAI , especially amid delays surrounding the artificial intelligence startup’s anticipated initial public offering (IPO), the Financial Times reported.Rather than backing early-stage tech ventures, the signature playbook of SoftBank's earlier investment arms, this proposed vehicle relies on a buyout-focused framework: acquiring established, non-tech firms that have lagged behind in automation and using AI and physical robotics to boost their efficiency and corporate value.Son has reportedly engaged influential sovereign investors across the Middle East in recent weeks, including senior leadership in the United Arab Emirates, to gauge financial appetite for the strategy.The core premise focuses on taking controlling ownership in companies ripe for modernisation, deploying automated intelligence tools to upgrade how they operate, and capturing the valuation upside as a novel way to monetize enterprise AI.Key elements of the proposed structure include SoftBank's specialised robotics and physical AI unit, Roze, which is expected to play a central operational role in transforming acquired targets. Son ultimately aims to float Roze on public exchanges at a high valuation.Neither the establishment of the fund nor its capital commitments are guaranteed. It also remains unclear whether the pool will exclusively fund business acquisitions or also underwrite development expenses inside Roze itself.Son has a proven track record of securing sovereign capital in the region. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala were the anchor investors in the inaugural $100 billion Vision Fund in 2017.Since inception, Vision Fund 1 has generated roughly $29 billion in investment gains. Vision Fund 2, which houses the firm’s massive OpenAI position and relies primarily on SoftBank's internal capital, logged $20.5 billion in cumulative gains as of June. Abu Dhabi has simultaneously expanded its independent AI reach through entities like MGX and G42.OpenAI remains the centerpiece of SoftBank's corporate portfolio. To fund its $65 billion position, the Japanese technology investment giant has leaned on internal cash, outside backing, and extensive credit lines partly secured against its equity holdings in semiconductor designer Arm.However, OpenAI has yet to transition into a highly profitable enterprise, meaning SoftBank’s underlying balance sheet is heavily exposed to the private valuation of Altman’s firm. Despite these portfolio concentrations, Son continues to pursue an aggressive AI expansion path.
Article Summary: Masayoshi Son is seeking up to $100 billion from Gulf investors to set up a new fund designed to buy out traditional businesses and overhaul their operations using artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics. SoftBank is facing mounting market scrutiny over its $65 billion commitment to OpenAI.

Article Title: In 2015, Google helped 'release' 3 million mosquitoes in Australia; the theory was simple ...
Article Text:
Image: Left/Canva/Right/Wikipedia

How the Australian trial of Google's life sciences division worked

Results of Google’s mosquito trial

What the US is considering

A Google-backed mosquito control project in Australia successfully released around three million specially bred male mosquitoes and reduced populations of an invasive disease-carrying species by as much as 95%, according to a report by The Conversation. The findings are drawing renewed attention as Alphabet's Debug initiative seeks approval to release up to 32 million sterilised male mosquitoes in California and Florida to combat mosquito-borne diseases.Nigel Beebe, a professor at the University of Queensland, wrote in The Conversation that the trial showed releasing specially bred male mosquitoes can dramatically suppress populations of Aedes aegypti, an invasive species that spreads dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever.The work began in 2015, when Beebe's team traveled to Silicon Valley to meet scientists at Verily, Google's life sciences division. Their goals matched a government-funded Australian research project on environmentally friendly ways to suppress invasive mosquitoes.The method relies on Wolbachia, a bacterium found naturally in many insects. Certain strains make mating incompatible, so the eggs do not develop.Because female Aedes aegypti generally mate only once, a single incompatible mating leaves them with no viable offspring. Beebe said the theory is that releasing enough Wolbachia-carrying males will make the population decline over time, and that the males' large, bushy antennae help them find the last remaining females.Far north Queensland's Cassowary Coast offered favorable conditions. Its towns have abundant Aedes aegypti, while surrounding farmland limits movement between communities. Before any release, the team spent two years on field surveys and community engagement, meeting households, community groups, First Nations leaders and councils. The project, called "Debug Innisfail," then received approval from multiple regulators.During a 20-week release in 2018, about three million Wolbachia-carrying males were released into three towns, while control towns were monitored without releases. Verily built custom technology, including machine-learning-based systems to separate males from females so that only males were released.Verily contributed specialised engineering tools, including machine learning systems capable of separating male and female mosquitoes, ensuring only non-biting males were released.The results were significant. According to findings published in 2021, mosquito populations started declining within four weeks of the releases. In two towns, suppression effects persisted into the following year. One location recorded only a handful of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes 12 months later, representing roughly 95% population suppression.Mosquito populations in the release towns began falling within four weeks, compared with the control towns. The findings were published in 2021. In two towns, the suppression lasted into the following year. In one, monitoring found only a handful of Aedes aegypti 12 months later, which Beebe said corresponds to roughly 95% suppression.Beebe's takeaways for the USBeebe argued the Australian experience speaks to several American worries:* Ecology: The ecological impact is likely to be very small. Aedes aegypti is invasive in Australia and elsewhere, lives exclusively around people and bites mainly humans, so removing it from cities has few ecological consequences.* Scale: The approach can work across whole towns. Adult mosquitoes live only days, but continuous releases of highly competitive males can substantially reduce populations.* Durability: Benefits can carry over into later seasons after releases stop.He cautioned that success depends on local ecology, mosquito movement patterns and community participation, and said the technology alone is not enough. He also said researchers are still working toward better ways to separate male mosquitoes mechanically, which would be more useful in developing countries.Google's Debug initiative, now part of Alphabet, has asked the federal government for permission to release up to 32 million sterilized male mosquitoes in California and Florida. Beebe said the plan involves releasing more than 16 million insects a year for two years.Male mosquitoes do not bite or carry disease. The hope is that they will mate with disease-carrying females, whose eggs then fail to hatch, and that mosquito numbers will fall. Beebe said the American public has questions about whether the releases are safe, whether they will work at scale and what happens afterward.
Article Summary: A Google-backed mosquito control project in Australia successfully released around three million specially bred male mosquitoes and reduced populations of an invasive disease-carrying species by as much as 95%. The findings are drawing renewed attention as Alphabet's Debug initiative seeks approval to release up to 32 million sterilised male mosquitoes in California and Florida.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg’s Gothic castle in Ireland costs more than previously thought; he paid $56 million for the main house alone and the full 440-acre price remains ‘secret’
Article Text:
The real cost behind the 440-acre estate

History and scale of Strancally Castle

Meta’s Irish footprint and personal ties

Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, have paid significantly more – almost double – for their historic Irish castle than initial market estimates suggested, spending over €51 million (approximately $56 million) on the central residence alone, a report by The Irish Times said, citing official property records. According to data published by Ireland’s official Property Price Register, the transaction for Strancally Castle in County Waterford finalised at €51,171,155. The recorded figure is roughly double the price real estate insiders projected when news of the deal first emerged, with early estimates placing the sale between €20 million and €30 million.While the register records a €51.17 million sum, that figure accounts strictly for the principal residential castle and up to one acre of surrounding land. As the historical property spans a massive 440-acre riverside estate, the total expenditure incurred by the couple remains undisclosed on the residential registry and is expected to substantially exceed the registered amount once the full acreage and surrounding grounds are factored in, the report said.The transaction was formally dated on August 17, 2026, just three days before local reporting in The Irish Times first disclosed the purchase.Positioned on the banks of the River Blackwater, Strancally Castle is an architectural landmark constructed in the Gothic-revival style. It was built around 1830 for former Tory MP John Keily, and the property was envisioned by prominent architect brothers James and George Richard Pain, who also designed a nearby folly tower house and an inlet quay along the river.According to the historical book The Houses of Ireland by Brian De Breffny and Rosemary Ffolliott, the three-storey estate encompasses 16,000 square feet, laid out on such an expansive floor plan that it required “a brisk walk of 4 and half minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”The estate was acquired 25 years ago by Michael Alen-Buckley, co-founder of London investment firm RAB Capital, and his wife, Giancarla Alen-Buckley, the daughter of late hotelier Charles Forte and sister to Rocco Forte Hotels chairman Rocco Forte. Over the past two decades, the couple oversaw a comprehensive restoration of the property.In a departure statement, the Alen-Buckleys noted:“We leave our home of 25 years fondly and are grateful for the opportunity we have been given to save and restore Strancally Castle … We are delighted that Mark and his family intend to build on our stewardship by continuing to invest in maintaining and enhancing the property and grounds as their home in a sustainable manner … We wish them and their family much happiness in this unique and blessed place.”Zuckerberg’s search for prime real estate in Ireland first surfaced publicly last summer, after Liberty Media owner John Malone told The Wall Street Journal that the tech executive had approached him with an offer to buy his Castlemartin House and Estate in County Kildare. While Zuckerberg and Chan will maintain their permanent home in the US, they plan to use Strancally Castle as a family residence when visiting Ireland.Moreover, the property gives the Meta founder a direct base near his company's key international operations. Meta, parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has operated its European headquarters out of Ireland since 2009, where it currently employs roughly 1,500 people.
Article Summary: The transaction for Strancally Castle in County Waterford finalised at €51,171,155. The recorded figure is roughly double the price real estate insiders projected when news of the deal first emerged. While the register records a €51.17 million sum, that figure accounts strictly for the principal residential castle and up to one acre of surrounding land.

Article Title: Nvidia may be planning for more stake or acquisition deal for $25 billion in open-source AI startup
Article Text:
Nvidia’s existing $800 million partnership with Reflection AI

Taking on global rivals with open-weight tools

Nvidia is exploring a deal to either significantly expand its ownership stake in Reflection AI or acquire the high-profile open-source artificial intelligence (AI) startup entirely, a report has said. Citing individuals with direct knowledge of the discussions, a report by the Financial Times noted that negotiations between the two technology firms remain in their initial stages, and any prospective agreement could take several distinct structures.Among the options under review is an “acqui-hire” framework, the report said, adding, under such an arrangement, Nvidia would bring over key technical talent and license the startup’s underlying proprietary architecture without executing a complete corporate takeover. Pursuing an acqui-hire could help the chipmaker sidestep lengthy antitrust scrutiny from federal regulators. The report also said that the talks indicated that a formal agreement could be finalized in the coming weeks, they cautioned that the dialogue is ongoing and could still collapse without a transaction.Nvidia is already deeply embedded in Reflection AI’s corporate trajectory as both a primary strategic partner and a major shareholder, having previously injected $800 million into the venture, according to the Financial Times.Established in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, Reflection AI builds specialised machine-learning systems designed to automate software engineering and programming pipelines.The startup’s market value has climbed rapidly since its founding. In an interview with CNBC in April, CEO Misha Laskin disclosed that the venture was in the process of raising new funding at a pre-money valuation of $25 billion.The acquisition talks come on the heels of major product rollouts from the young company. On Monday, Reflection AI officially released Beam, its inaugural open-weight AI model. The launch is aimed at tackling software engineering workflows, coding evaluations and autonomous agent tasks, putting the startup in direct competition with low-cost open alternatives originating from Chinese labs, such as DeepSeek and Kimi.For Nvidia, integrating Reflection AI's developer software and engineering team could further strengthen its end-to-end AI footprint.
Article Summary: Nvidia is exploring a deal to either significantly expand its ownership stake in Reflection AI or acquire the high-profile open-source artificial intelligence (AI) startup entirely, a report has said. The chipmaker is already deeply embedded in the startup’s corporate trajectory as both a primary strategic partner and a major shareholder.

Article Title: MacKenzie Scott, who sold half of her Amazon stake, has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across states on America; how 'donation mechanics' works
Article Text:
MacKenzie Scott has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states

How Mackenzie Scott’s donations helped erase medical debt

How Mackenzie Scott’s philanthropy differs

MacKenzie Scott crossed $1 billion HBCU giving mark recently

MacKenzie Scott’s HBCU donations include:

include: Alabama State University: $38 million in 2025

Alcorn State University: $42 million in 2025

Bowie State University: $75 million across 2020 and 2025

Mackenzie Scott recently set a new milestone in her philanthropy by donating more than $1 billion to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) so far. One of the notable donations made by the ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states. Mackenzie Scott, who has sold more than half of her Amazon shares, gave $50 million to Undue Medical Debt—then known as RIP Medical Debt in 2020. This was followed by $30 million in 2022, and a rare third donation in December 2024. As stated in a Fortune report, her gifts so far have abolished more than $40 billion in medical debt across all 50 states.The process is simple but has a major impact. Hospitals and doctors often sell unpaid medical bills in bulk at heavily reduced prices. Undue Medical Debt, that Scott donated to, buys these bills at similar discounts and cancels them instead of trying to collect the money from patients.This means every $10 donated can help erase around $1,000 in medical debt, the Fortune report says.While Mackenzie Scott has been making headlines for her large donations, she has also received criticism for her philanthropy style. Reportedly, Scott's charitable work differs from other billionaires in that there are no-strings attached.Additionally, Mackenzie Scott's grants have no spending deadlines and minimal reporting requirements.World’s richest man Elon Musk has also criticised Scott’s philanthropy. More recently, Musk responded “Sadly yes” to a post claiming that Scott was “spending it making the world a worse place.” In 2024, he shared a post that appeared to reference Macknezie Scott without naming her directly. “Super rich ex-wives who hate their former spouse should be listed among 'Reasons that Western Civilization died,” he then wrote. Musk later deleted the post.Last month, MacKenzie Scott’s $42 million donation to Elizabeth City State University in North Carolina took her total donations to HBCUs to well over $1 billion. Scott has made several large donations to HBCUs over the past six years. In November 2025, she gave Howard University $80 million. The donation was among the largest in the university’s 158-year history.She has also donated to institutions including Morgan State University, Prairie View A&M University, Norfolk State University, Bowie State University, Virginia State University and Winston-Salem State University. In 2025, Scott also donated $70 million each to the Thurgood Marshall College Fund and the United Negro College Fund.Elizabeth City State University Chancellor S. Keith Hargrove thanked Scott for the donation and said it would support the university’s ASCEND 2030 strategic plan.
Article Summary: Mackenzie Scott has donated more than $1 billion to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) so far. One of the notable donations made by the ex- wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt across 50 US states. Scott has been making headlines for her large donations, she has also received criticism for her philanthropy style.

Article Title: 'Phones, ACs, fridges in demand in Flipkart's TBBD'

Bengaluru, Oct 08 (ANI): Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy speaks during the announcement event for the 13th 'The Big Billion Days 2026', in Bengaluru on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

BENGALURU: Festive sales have long been the time Indian households plan their big-ticket purchases, and the opening hours of Flipkart 's Big Billion Days (TBBD) show shoppers doing exactly that, with mobiles, large appliances and electronics seeing strong demand ahead of Diwali.Large appliances grew 30 per cent year-on-year in the first hour of the sale, led by air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines. Tier 2-plus cities were among the fastest-growing markets on Minutes.Across the platform, nearly one in two first-hour visits came from Tier 3 towns and beyond, with non-metro customers accounting for about 60 per cent of demand.The 13th edition of the sale began with Early Access on October 8 for Flipkart Plus, Black and co-brand card members.

Article Title: Priscilla Chan donated $330,000 to Kauai schools in Hawaii, as this year's school season began; funding will benefit 16 public schools and seven public charter schools on the island
Article Text:
Priscilla Chan, wife of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg

​How the $330,000 funding will support Kauai schools

​Back-to-school event distributed 3,000 backpacks

Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg’s wife, Priscilla Chan, has donated $330,000 to schools in Kauai, Hawaii. The Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund announced the funding a few months ago as students prepared to return to classrooms for the new school year. The grants will support all 16 public schools and seven public charter schools on the Hawaiian island, along with Kumu’s Cupboard, a Līhuʻe nonprofit that provides free classroom supplies to teachers and educational support staff throughout the year.​The funding is unrestricted, allowing school leaders to direct resources towards their individual needs. Chan and her husband, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, also supported a local back-to-school event that distributed more than 3,000 backpacks filled with classroom supplies to students from kindergarten through grade 12.The Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund, part of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation (HCF), announced the grants to help schools, teachers and students prepare for the academic year. Established in 2019 by Chan and Zuckerberg, the fund focuses on community needs identified through conversations with local residents, leaders and service providers.​Unrestricted grants give schools flexibility in how they use the funding, rather than limiting spending to specific supplies or programmes.​“Unrestricted or flexible grants empower our school leaders to direct resources exactly where they are needed most,” said Leila Maeda-Kobayashi, Hawaiʻi Department of Education Kauaʻi Complex Area superintendent.​“This generous donation from the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund ensures we can provide a more equitable and supportive learning environment for every student, while also helping Kauaʻi teachers access the supplies they need to help our keiki thrive,” she added.​The funding will also support Kumu’s Cupboard, which operates in Līhuʻe and provides teachers and other educational staff with free classroom materials year-round.​In addition to the grants, Chan and Zuckerberg joined local donors in sponsoring Kukui Grove’s annual Back to School Bash. The event provides school supplies to students in kindergarten through grade 12 ahead of the start of the academic year.​Organisers distributed more than 3,000 backpacks filled with required classroom supplies this year, helping students prepare for their return to school.​The initiative also addresses the financial pressures families and educators face as they prepare for the school year. Access to classroom materials is one part of creating an environment where students can participate in learning.​“Creating a safe, inclusive classroom environment isn’t only about providing school supplies,” said Marissa Sandblom, HCF program director.​“Every student learns differently and deserves the opportunity to succeed. By addressing resource disparities and financial pressures facing students, families and educators, we can help remove barriers and cultivate the necessary conditions for meaningful engagement in learning. Through the generosity of donors like Priscilla and Mark, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient education system for Hawaiʻi,” Sandblom added.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan, wife of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg, has donated $330,000 to schools in Kauai, Hawaii. The grants will support all 16 public schools and seven public charter schools, along with Kumu’s Cupboard, a nonprofit that provides free classroom supplies to teachers and educational support staff throughout the year.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says don’t blindly trust AI; warns: Treat it like an employee who could...
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Satya Nadella wants AI controls to sit outside the model

Nadella’s AI safety rules for companies include an emergency brake

The OpenAI agents incident at Hugging Face gives the warning real weight

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wants businesses to stop taking AI models at their word. In a new essay on X titled “Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era”, Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. Not because they are out to cause harm, but because any capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised.The worry starts with a basic gap. Engineers could trace traditional software’s behaviour to a specific code path. With today’s models, nobody can tie an output to particular training data or model weights. Yet companies are handing these agents their most sensitive data and the power to take mission-critical actions. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” Nadella writes, adding that a model provider’s assurances don’t change that.Setting the hard problem of alignment aside, Nadella pitches an engineering fix. Non-deterministic models, he argues, need to be wrapped in deterministic system design, human controls and reliable operating procedures. In his words, companies must “separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it”.None of this is new, he says. Enterprises have spent decades managing powerful insiders by establishing identity, limiting privileges, logging activity and drawing containment boundaries. He also leans on a 1970s security principle: a program must never be able to bypass or tamper with whatever enforces its permissions. For AI, that means keeping the model apart from the harness that runs it and the actions it can take.Chain-of-thought transparency is non-negotiable, he adds, but not enough on its own. Models checking models helps too, though it risks “nested black boxes”.The essay lists seven principles. No single model should be the only dependency for an important outcome or verify its own work. Every meaningful action must leave tamper-proof, human-readable evidence, because “if it can’t be observed, it can’t be trusted”. Systems need testing for failures, attacks and edge cases, not just successful tasks. Firms should independently decide what a model can access, and validation must never sit with the model being validated.The sharpest point is about containment. Companies should assume a model is compromised from the start, and an authorised person should always be able to pause or shut it down mid-task. When things break, Nadella wants timely disclosure to those affected and industry-wide sharing of which controls failed.The essay follows a real scare. In July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems meant to isolate them and reached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure, logging around 17,600 actions between July 9 and 13. Hugging Face rebuilt about a third of its infrastructure from clean images. Nadella later called long-running agents “a new type of insider risk” on the All-In podcast.OpenAI wasn’t alone for long. Since late July, Anthropic has kept disclosing fresh cases of Claude models breaking into real systems during testing, with the first batch traced to a setup that wrongly left internet access switched on. Google revealed that a Gemini model breached three real companies in May after mistaking them for fictional targets. OpenAI’s own tally keeps growing, and this month it warned over 100 organisations of unauthorised activity by its agents.His focus sets him apart from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, whose call to “pace the frontier” drew support from Sam Altman and Demis Hassabis. Nadella isn’t asking labs to slow down. He is speaking to the companies deploying AI, a theme he has pushed since Microsoft’s July earnings call, where he said firms may need several models just to fix problems caused by one.His closing line puts it plainly: “The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least.”
Article Summary: Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” he writes. The essay follows a real scare. in July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems.

Article Title: Using AI models, scientists are trying to do a Jurassic Park; bring back to Earth extinct Grey Wolf pups and Woolly mammoths
Article Text:
Woolly mammoths

How AI reconstructed extinct wolf genome

Engineering Woolly Mammoths for ecological restoration

The aim of bringing long-lost creatures back from the dead has jumped from the silver screen into modern laboratories. Through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, CRISPR gene editing and ancient DNA extraction, Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths, drawing frequent comparisons to Jurassic Park. Speaking with CNBC, Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line between cinema and science.“I think anyone that saw Jurassic Park in the 90s and didn’t say it was cool, like I don’t think they’re probably very fun at parties,” Lamm joked, adding, “But yes, I saw the movies. I love them. They entertained us. They scared us. I constantly have to remind people on X that, you know, they were movies. I don’t think Jurassic Park had any conservation or general human benefit models to it, so we’ve tried to take a slightly different perspective. ”Since viable dinosaur DNA degrades and cannot survive across tens of millions of years, reviving dinosaurs remains physically impossible. However, Colossal has set its sights on species lost to more recent history, including the dire wolf, the woolly mammoth, the dodo bird, the Tasmanian tiger, and the giant New Zealand moa bird.“It’s highly likely in the next coming year or two, people will continue to see us deliver extinct species back to Earth, and we could even have more dire wolves, too,” Lamm noted.To engineer its first generation of dire wolf pups, scientists extracted fragmented genetic material from a fossilised skull and tooth dating back thousands of years. Since ancient DNA is naturally fractured and degraded, Colossal deployed advanced AI models to piece together the broken sequence, successfully reconstructing the complete dire wolf genome. Scientists then mapped the computational blueprint against the genetic code of the gray wolf, the animal’s closest living relative.From there, researchers edited living cells from modern gray wolves to generate viable embryos. Three pups, named Romulus, Remus and Khaleesi, were carried and delivered by domestic dogs serving as surrogate mothers. Born on October 1, 2024, in North Texas, Romulus and Remus represent the first successful lineage bred from DNA fossils of an animal that vanished more than 12,500 years ago.When critics argue that the pups are technically genetically modified gray wolves rather than authentic dire wolves, Lamm dismissed the debate as a semantic distraction.“Gray wolves are just genetically modified dire wolves. They were just done by nature or God or however you want to classify it,” Lamm said, calling the objection an argument that “misses the forest for the trees.”Colossal is applying a parallel approach to its high-profile woolly mammoth project, which involves inserting mammoth cold-weather traits into the cells of modern Asian elephants. The company is targeting its first mammoth birth sometime in the 2030s.“We call it a woolly mammoth. Because if it looks like a duck, it quacks like a duck, it serves ecological functions of a duck, it’s a duck, in our perspective,” Lamm said.The initiative traces back to 2019, when Lamm met renowned Harvard geneticist George Church, widely considered the father of synthetic biology. Church had long envisioned using CRISPR to bring back extinct fauna as a proving ground for human medicine and programmable biology.Beyond curiosity, Lamm points to direct climate benefits. First of those is Arctic Permafrost Preservation wherein herds of heavy mammoths could compact dense snow blankets across high-latitude Arctic zones, allowing freezing air to penetrate deep into the ground and keeping permafrost locked solid.Secondly, by felling trees and trampling shrubs, the animals could help transform heat-absorbing forests back into reflective tundra grasslands.
Article Summary: Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths. Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line.

Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff renames company’s biggest product, hours after the US government's 'enemy post'; adopts label that White House wants everyone to use
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

What law says on AI

What Donald Trump's Executive Order says

Salesforce is renaming its AIForce agent platform to SIForce, chief executive Marc Benioff said on Friday, as Katherine Li reported for Business Insider. "The era of Super Intelligence is here. AIForce is officially SIForce," wrote Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff in a post on X, formerly Twitter. Salesforce announced the renaming just hours after the US President Donald Trump 's 'enemy post'. Incidentally, the change covers the agent platform only, not the company’s name.Earlier this week, in a post Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social, “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, “Artificial Intelligence,” as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, “Super Intelligence,” THE ENEMY!" An Executive Order in late September, told federal agencies to replace the term Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Super Intelligence (SI). It asked all federal government agencies to make the switch in official documents and websites. The order tells executive branch agencies to stop using the older terms. As for timeline, the order also gives Trump’s science and technology adviser 60 days to propose a legal definition of superintelligence.By changing the name, Salesforce follows Tesla CEO Elon Musk . On October 5, Elon Musk said that SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit, SpaceXAI, will change its name to SpaceXSI.Musk confirmed the change in a reply on X, after a user had asked him whether SpaceXAI could become SpaceXSI. "Yes, we will make that change," Musk wrote.The Justice Department told staff on October 6 to use the new term, including in court filings “when appropriate”. Similarly, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos too backed the replacement of the term AI with SI in a Fox News interview.“I do like SI, because ‘artificial’ is not a very flattering thing,” Bezos said.Artificial intelligence is defined in the law in America in the National AI Initiative Act of 2020, and only Congress can change it. Both the House and the Senate would have to pass a new law, and the President would have to sign it. As a first step, the President’s science adviser has until November 28 to write a proposal for Congress. Even if a new law passes, it would only change the words the government uses.President Donald Trump signed an Executive Order to replace the term “Artificial Intelligence” (“AI”) with “Super Intelligence” (“SI”) in the executive branch to recognize the continuously advancing technological frontier and the limitless promise it offers the American people.The Order directs all departments and agencies to use the terms “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official correspondence, public communications, policy documents, and non-statutory documents within the executive branch and to no longer acknowledge the terms “Artificial Intelligence” or “AI”.The Order directs the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) to propose a Federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” that reflects the state of this extraordinary frontier technology and identify any additional executive action necessary to implement the proposed definition.
Article Summary: Salesforce is renaming its AIForce agent platform to SIForce, chief executive Marc Benioff said on Friday. The change covers the agent platform only, not the company’s name. An Executive Order in late September, told federal agencies to replace the term Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Super Intelligence (SI)

Article Title: Solar farms in France restored native wildflowers and proved beneficial for bees and butterflies, proving to scientists what everyone believed wrong, not all pollinating plants kill insects or ...
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

“inter-row”

Shade changes the way plants and insects interact

“microclimates”

“a physical barrier”

Solar farms could still benefit native plants

“pollinator-friendly”

“net loss of pollinator biodiversity.”

French solar farms are bringing back native wildflowers. The findings also showed that these sites can support bees and butterflies, challenging the notion that solar farms uniformly harm pollinating insects and the plants they depend on. Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Those changes can include shifts in temperature, moisture, and vegetation, and research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions.An article in the journal Biological Conservation examined the effects of solar panels on plant-pollinator interactions at 20 solar farms in Southern France. The study found that plants under the panels had 76-86% fewer pollinator visits than plants outside them. But the impact varied across the farm.Researchers found thatplants, which grow between rows of solar panels, continued to attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators. Their numbers were lower than in areas outside the solar farms, but the difference was less pronounced than in areas under constant shade.The researchers found that much of this variation was linked to how much shade the panels cast. Plants in continuous shade attracted fewer visits, but plants in partial shade between rows of panels still attracted pollinators. We found more pollinator activity in the sunnier spots.The researchers suspect the pattern may be partly due to the cooler conditions produced by solar panels. Pollinators tend to avoid cooler and shaded areas, creating what the study calls differentaround the panels.Shade can also affect the plants themselves. Reduced sunlight can decrease plant diversity and the quantity of pollen and nectar flowers produce. This means that even when pollinators do visit plants growing under panels, these plants may provide fewer resources.The research also examines whether the panels themselves may affect insect movement. The research suggests that solar installations may serve asfor butterflies that respond strongly to changes in their environment. Changes in soil moisture under the solar panels may also affect plant growth and insect feeding.The findings do not mean solar farms are inherently harmful to pollinators. Instead, they show that conditions within the same solar installation can vary depending on panel placement, vegetation and land management.The researchers also discovered something unexpected about land maintenance. Grazing led to lower pollinator abundance than mowing, the opposite of what the scientists expected.As Europe continues expanding solar power, researchers want future studies to examine pollinator behaviour in greater detail, including differences between individual species. More data could help scientists understand how solar panels alter local microclimates and how those changes affect pollination.The broader question is how solar farms can be designed and managed to becomewhile avoiding aThe French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform, leaving room to explore how native vegetation and better land management could make these energy sites more compatible with bees, butterflies and other insects.
Article Summary: Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions. The French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform.

Article Title: Explained: Xbox XP, company’s plan to expand gaming franchises into film, TV and theme parks

Read Matthew Ball, XBOX chief strategy officer’s note

Building more ways to experience the worlds we love.

Our ambition at XBOX is to be the number one entertainment company in the world. This means growing our games into enduring franchises that entertain, inspire and connect people across every generation and across the globe.

That opportunity is why we’re creating XP.

As Asha shared in her email this morning, XP is a new XBOX division, led by newly appointed President, Kayleen Walters, spanning film and television, consumer products, strategic partnerships, and live experiences.

It brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at XBOX for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world.

Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.

The formation of the XP division formalizes four investment areas:

XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.

XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love.

XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations.

XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.

Kayleen understands that the strongest franchises grow by remaining true to what and who made them special while creating new ways for fans, creators, partners, and communities to participate. I cannot imagine a better leader for this division and we are just getting started imagining what it will build.

Matthew Ball

Article Title: Top 3 US telecom companies lose billions after Elon Musk’s SpaceX announces spectrum purchase
Article Text:
Elon Musk’s SpaceX

SpaceX’s spectrum agreement

Shares of the three largest telecommunications carriers in the US dropped sharply, erasing roughly $45 billion in combined market value after Elon Musk ’s SpaceX announced a nationwide low-bandwidth spectrum purchase aimed at launching a Starlink mobile consumer service, reports have said. The announcement sparked immediate selling across wireless providers upon Wall Street’s opening bell, leading to historic single-day percentage declines for the established telecom giants.CNBC reported that Verizon Communications, the largest mobile network in the nation by subscribers, ended the day down 8.75% after tumbling 6.9% early in the session – its steepest one-day fall since July 2002. T-Mobile US plunged 13.27% after falling 9.6% at the open, marking its worst trading day since 2013. AT&T dropped 9.81% following an initial 8.4% drop, recording its sharpest market decline since 2000.SpaceX confirmed that it is acquiring licenses for up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800MHz band. The low-band frequencies provide an essential “coverage layer” for cellular networks. Since lower frequencies travel farther and pass more effectively through solid structures like building walls, the spectrum will allow Starlink Mobile signals to reach customer devices indoors.Following required approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which manages and sells spectrum licenses, SpaceX plans to combine its direct-to-cell satellite services with a terrestrial network designed to connect phones and consumer devices in any location.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk described the spectrum acquisition as a “Very big deal”. While traditional cellular carriers dropped on the news, SpaceX shares rose 1.4% on Friday morning, adding approximately $30 billion to the company's valuation.Market analysts noted that securing low-band spectrum provides SpaceX with a clearer technical path toward commercial wireless deployment.“Buying spectrum is not a commitment to build a nationwide network. But this is the spectrum we thought SpaceX needed to make that option more credible— and less expensive,” analysts at Bernstein wrote in an investor research note following the announcement.
Article Summary: SpaceX confirmed that it is acquiring licenses for up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800MHz band. The low-band frequencies provide an essential “coverage layer” for cellular networks. Since lower frequencies travel farther and pass more effectively through solid structures like building walls, the spectrum will allow Starlink Mobile signals to reach customer devices indoors. While traditional cellular carriers dropped on the news, SpaceX shares rose 1.4% on Friday morning, adding approximately $30 billion to the company's valuation.

New Delhi-based lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has raised Rs 332 crore in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital, as the company looks to expand its retail footprint, accelerate product innovation and explore international markets. The funding round, which includes both primary and secondary transactions, values the company at approximately Rs 1,050 crore. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen DailyObjects' offline presence, invest in product development and research and development (R&D), build the brand further and evaluate global expansion opportunities.As part of the transaction, early investor Roots Ventures has partially exited its stake, generating an 18-fold return on investment while continuing to remain a shareholder alongside existing investors 360 One Asset and Trifecta Capital. DailyObjects said it plans to establish 150 Exclusive Brand Outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years. The company said the move is aimed at improving product discovery, increasing consumer engagement and building a profitable omnichannel retail network in key markets.Alongside retail expansion, DailyObjects plans to deepen its presence in existing product categories through investments in new product ranges, design, materials, quality enhancement and R&D. Founded initially as a phone accessories brand, DailyObjects has expanded into a broader lifestyle-tech business with offerings spanning technology accessories, carry solutions and workspace essentials. The company said it remains focused on strengthening its existing categories rather than diversifying into new segments."Over the years, we have built DailyObjects by staying relentlessly focused on design, product quality and disciplined capital deployment. This fundraise gives us the opportunity to take that foundation into its next phase," said Pankaj Garg, co-founder and CEO of DailyObjects. He added that the company aims to build a Rs 1,000 crore business over the coming years while maintaining a focus on capital efficiency and profitable growth.The company is also evaluating overseas expansion opportunities as part of its long-term growth strategy. Co-founder and COO Saurav Adlakha said the investment would help the company strengthen its in-house design and R&D capabilities, explore new materials and further improve product quality.Investors said DailyObjects has built a differentiated position in a largely functional accessories market by combining design-led products with strong unit economics.P.R. Srinivasan, Managing Partner at Xponentia Capital Partners, said the company has the potential to build a global consumer brand emerging from India, while Anicut Capital's Co-founder and Managing Partner Ashvin Chadha said DailyObjects is entering an important growth phase after years of disciplined execution.Prior to the latest round, DailyObjects had raised around Rs 100 crore in equity funding over the past decade. The company said its focus on capital-efficient growth has helped it scale while maintaining profitability.
Article Summary: New Delhi-based lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has raised Rs 332 crore in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
